recipes.name: Idli
steps: Measure idli rice and urad dal
Wash idli rice three times in water
Wash urad dal three times in water
Soak idli rice in water for 6 hours
Soak urad dal and fenugreek seeds for 6 hours
Drain water from urad dal
Grind urad dal with little water into smooth paste
Drain water from rice
Grind rice into slightly coarse paste
Mix both pastes in a bowl
Add salt and mix well
Cover and ferment for 8 hours
Grease idli plates with oil
Pour batter into moulds
Heat water in steamer on high flame
Place plates inside
Steam for 10 minutes on medium flame
Turn off the flame
Rest for 2 minutes
Extract idlis using a spoon

recipes.name: Masala Dosa
steps: Boil potatoes in water until tender
Peel and mash potatoes
Wash and chop onion and green chilli
Heat pan on medium flame and add oil
Add mustard seeds and let splutter
Add onion and green chilli; sauté until translucent
Add turmeric and salt
Add mashed potato and mix well
Cook filling for 3 minutes then turn off the flame
Heat dosa pan on medium flame
Pour dosa batter and spread into a thin disc
Drizzle oil around edges
Cook until the base is crisp and golden
Place potato filling in center
Fold the dosa and transfer to a plate

recipes.name: Plain Dosa
steps: Heat dosa pan on medium flame
Pour dosa batter in center
Spread batter in a circular motion
Drizzle oil around edges
Cook until bottom turns golden brown
Flip dosa gently
Cook for 30 seconds
Transfer to a serving plate

recipes.name: Set Dosa
steps: Pour thick, small dosas and cook one side covered to make them spongy.
Grind coconut, fennel seeds, and green chillies into a smooth paste.
Boil mixed vegetables; add the coconut-fennel paste and salt; simmer.
Add a squeeze of fresh lemon juice for tanginess.
Turn off the flame and serve the spongy dosas with kurma.

recipes.name: Rava Idli
steps: Dry roast rava on low flame until aromatic
Allow rava to cool completely
Wash and grate carrot
Chop green chilli finely
Heat pan on medium flame with oil and mustard seeds
Add carrot and chilli; sauté briefly
Add roasted rava and salt
Mix in curd and water to form a thick batter
Rest batter for 10 minutes
Grease idli plates
Pour batter into moulds
Steam for 10 minutes
Turn off the flame and rest before serving

recipes.name: Khara Bath
steps: Dry roast rava on low flame
Wash and chop vegetables into small cubes
Heat pan on medium flame with oil and mustard seeds
Add onion and green chilli; sauté until soft
Add vegetables and sauté for 2 minutes
Add water and salt
Bring water to a rolling boil
Add rava slowly while stirring to avoid lumps
Cook on low flame for 5 minutes
Turn off the flame
Rest for 2 minutes before serving

recipes.name: Kesari Bath
steps: Heat ghee in pan on medium flame
Add rava and roast lightly until golden
Add boiling water and stir
Cook until rava absorbs water and becomes soft
Add sugar and cardamom powder
Mix continuously to dissolve sugar
Cook until the mixture thickens and leaves sides
Turn off the flame

recipes.name: Poori
steps: Add wheat flour and salt to a mixing bowl
Add water gradually and knead into a stiff dough
Rest dough for 10 minutes
Divide dough into small lemon-sized balls
Roll balls into flat circles
Heat oil on high flame for deep frying
Fry poori until it puffs up and turns golden
Drain excess oil and serve hot

recipes.name: Upma
steps: Dry roast rava on low flame
Chop onion and green chilli
Heat pan on medium flame with oil and mustard seeds
Add onion and chilli; sauté well
Add water and salt; bring to a boil
Add rava slowly while stirring
Cook for 5 minutes on low heat
Turn off the flame

recipes.name: Avalakki Uppittu
steps: Wash poha and drain water immediately
Chop onion and green chilli
Heat pan on medium flame; add oil and peanuts
Sauté onion and chilli until soft
Add poha and salt
Mix gently to avoid mashing
Cook for 3 minutes
Turn off the flame

recipes.name: Neer Dosa
steps: Wash rice three times
Soak rice for 4 hours
Drain water completely
Grind rice with water into a very thin, watery batter
Add salt and mix
Heat pan on medium flame
Pour batter quickly without spreading
Cover and cook for 1 minute
Transfer dosa to a plate carefully

recipes.name: Akki Rotti
steps: Wash and chop vegetables finely
Add rice flour, vegetables, and salt to a bowl
Add water and mix to a soft dough
Heat pan on medium flame
Spread dough thinly onto the pan by hand
Drizzle oil around edges
Cook both sides until crisp
Transfer to a plate

recipes.name: Ragi Rotti
steps: Chop onion and green chilli finely
Add ragi flour, vegetables, and salt to a bowl
Add water and mix to a pliable dough
Heat pan on medium flame
Spread dough thinly onto the pan
Drizzle oil and cook both sides
Transfer to a plate when cooked through

recipes.name: Bisi Bele Bath
steps: Fresh Powder: Dry roast chana dal, urad dal, coriander seeds, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, marathi moggu, and byadagi chillies; grind with dry coconut into a fine powder.
Pressure cook rice and toor dal with turmeric until very soft.
Cook chopped carrot, french beans, and green peas in water until tender.
Extract thick tamarind juice and add the prepared fresh spice powder and salt.
Boil the tamarind mixture until the raw aroma disappears.
Mix the cooked rice-dal mash and vegetables into the liquid base.
Simmer for 5 minutes, adding ghee-fried cashews and mustard seeds.
Turn off the flame and serve hot with boondi.

recipes.name: Vangi Bath
steps: Fresh Powder: Dry roast chana dal, coriander seeds, 2 cloves, a small cinnamon stick, and 4 red chillies; grind into a coarse powder.
Cook rice grains so they are separate and spread to cool.
Sauté peanuts, mustard seeds, and sliced green brinjal in oil.
Add the prepared spice powder, salt, and a dash of tamarind juice.
Cook until brinjal is soft and the oil separates from the masala.
Gently fold the cooled rice into the brinjal masala.
Turn off the flame and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Tomato Bath
steps: Wash rice and cook
Wash and chop tomato and onion
Heat pan on medium flame; sauté onion until brown
Add tomato and cook until mushy
Add spice powder and salt
Add cooked rice and mix well
Turn off the flame

recipes.name: Chow Chow Bath
steps: Prepare savory Khara Bath in one pan
Prepare sweet Kesari Bath in another pan
Serve equal portions side by side on a plate

recipes.name: Holige
steps: Soak chana dal for 2 hours
Cook dal until soft and drain
Mash dal and mix with jaggery to make filling
Make a soft dough with maida
Stuff dal filling into dough balls
Roll gently into thin discs
Cook on pan with ghee until golden
Transfer to a plate

recipes.name: Kharabath
steps: Dry roast rava on low heat
Cook chopped vegetables until tender
Add water, spices, and salt; bring to a boil
Add roasted rava slowly while stirring
Cook until thick and fluffy
Turn off the flame

recipes.name: Uddina Vada
steps: Wash and soak urad dal for 4 hours
Drain water completely
Grind dal into a thick, fluffy batter
Add onion, chilli, and salt; mix well
Heat oil for deep frying
Shape batter into donuts and fry until golden
Drain oil and serve

recipes.name: Maddur Vada
steps: Chop onion and green chilli finely
Mix rice flour, vegetables, and salt in a bowl
Add a little water and mix into a stiff dough
Heat oil on medium flame
Flatten small portions of dough and deep fry
Fry until crisp and golden brown
Drain excess oil

recipes.name: Buns
steps: Mash overripe banana in a bowl
Add sugar and curd; whisk well
Add maida and knead into a dough
Rest dough for 6 hours
Heat oil for deep frying
Roll dough and fry until puffed and golden
Drain excess oil

recipes.name: Kotte Kadubu
steps: Grind fresh coconut and jaggery into a paste
Add salt and mix
Prepare a pliable rice flour dough
Fill coconut mixture inside jackfruit leaf cones
Steam for 15 minutes
Turn off the flame and serve

recipes.name: Pathrode
steps: Wash colocasia leaves and pat dry
Soak rice for 4 hours and grind with coconut and spices
Apply spice paste on leaves and stack them
Roll leaves tightly and steam for 20 minutes
Slice the rolls and shallow fry until crisp
Turn off the flame and serve

recipes.name: Goli Baje
steps: Mix maida, curd, chopped chillies, and ginger in a bowl
Add salt and whisk to a thick, dropping consistency
Rest the batter for 2 hours
Heat oil for deep frying
Drop small balls of batter into hot oil
Fry until golden and fluffy
Drain excess oil and turn off the flame

recipes.name: Bisi Bele Bath
steps: Fresh Powder: Dry roast chana dal, urad dal, coriander seeds, cumin, cloves, cinnamon, marathi moggu, and byadagi chillies; grind with dry coconut into a fine powder.
Pressure cook rice and toor dal with turmeric until very soft.
Cook chopped carrot, french beans, and green peas in water until tender.
Extract thick tamarind juice and add the prepared fresh spice powder and salt.
Boil the tamarind mixture until the raw aroma disappears.
Mix the cooked rice-dal mash and vegetables into the liquid base.
Simmer for 5 minutes, adding ghee-fried cashews and mustard seeds.
Turn off the flame and serve hot with boondi.

recipes.name: Vangi Bath
steps: Fresh Powder: Dry roast chana dal, coriander seeds, 2 cloves, a small cinnamon stick, and 4 red chillies; grind into a coarse powder.
Cook rice grains so they are separate and spread to cool.
Sauté peanuts, mustard seeds, and sliced green brinjal in oil.
Add the prepared spice powder, salt, and a dash of tamarind juice.
Cook until brinjal is soft and the oil separates from the masala.
Gently fold the cooled rice into the brinjal masala.
Turn off the flame and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Sambar (Huli)
steps: Fresh Paste: Roast coriander seeds, cumin, a few fenugreek seeds, and red chillies; grind with fresh coconut and water into a smooth paste.
Pressure cook dal until mushy; boil drumstick, pumpkin, and carrot until tender.
Mix tamarind juice, salt, jaggery, and the fresh ground paste in a pot.
Add cooked dal and vegetables; boil for 10 minutes until the flavors meld.
Temper with mustard seeds, curry leaves, and hing in ghee.
Turn off the flame and serve with hot rice.

recipes.name: Saaru (Rasam)
steps: Fresh Spice Mix: Coarsely crush black pepper, cumin, and coriander seeds with 3 cloves of garlic using a mortar and pestle.
Boil mashed tomatoes and tamarind water with turmeric and salt.
Stir in the fresh crushed spice mix and a small piece of jaggery.
Simmer until it froths up; do not allow it to reach a hard boil.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in ghee.
Turn off the flame immediately.

recipes.name: Majjige Huli
steps: Boil ash gourd pieces in water with turmeric and salt until soft.
Fresh Paste: Grind coconut, green chilli, cumin, and soaked chana dal into a smooth, thick paste.
Whisk curd and mix with the ground paste.
Add this mixture to the cooked gourd and heat gently on low flame.
Turn off the flame before it reaches a boil to prevent curdling.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.

recipes.name: Beans Palya
steps: Temper mustard seeds, urad dal, and green chillies in oil.
Add finely chopped french beans and salt with a splash of water.
Cover and steam-cook until the beans are tender.
Add fresh grated coconut and toss well.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Ennegayi (Stuffed Brinjal)
steps: Fresh Masala: Dry roast peanuts, sesame, and niger seeds; grind with garlic, onions, and red chilli powder into a thick paste.
Stuff the slit small purple brinjals with this ground masala.
Heat oil in a pan and sauté onions until brown.
Place stuffed brinjals in the pan and slow-cook with a lid until tender.
Add remaining masala paste and tamarind water; simmer until oil floats on top.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Hesaru Bele Thove
steps: Pressure cook moong dal with turmeric and grated ginger until very soft.
Mash the dal lightly; add salt and slit green chillies.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in ghee.
Add fresh lemon juice for a tangy finish.
Turn off the flame and serve with hot rice.

recipes.name: Avarekalu Pulao
steps: Grind mint, coriander, and green chillies with coconut into a green paste.
Sauté whole spices and hyacinth beans (avarekalu) in oil.
Add the green paste, soaked rice, and water.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles until fluffy.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Mente Pulao
steps: Sauté onions and ginger-garlic paste until brown.
Add fresh chopped methi (fenugreek) leaves and spices.
Stir in washed rice and double the amount of water.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Gojju Avalakki
steps: Soak poha in a mixture of tamarind juice, jaggery, and rasam powder.
Prepare a tempering with mustard, peanuts, and curry leaves.
Mix the soaked poha into the tempering.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Heerekayi Thogave
steps: Pressure cook ridge gourd and toor dal until soft.
Grind coconut and tamarind into a paste and add to the gourd mixture.
Simmer for 5 minutes and add a mustard tempering.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Bendekayi Palya
steps: Wash ladys finger, dry completely with a cloth, and chop into rounds.
Heat oil, add mustard seeds, and fry ladys finger on medium heat.
Add a teaspoon of tamarind juice to remove the sliminess.
Sauté until crisp and add salt only at the very end.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Gorikayi Palya
steps: Steam chopped cluster beans until tender.
Toss with grated coconut, a bit of jaggery, and salt.
Temper with mustard seeds and dry red chillies.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Basale Soppu Gasi
steps: Boil malabar spinach and mangalore cucumber pieces together until soft.
Fresh Paste: Grind fresh coconut with roasted red chillies and tamarind.
Mix the paste into the boiled vegetables and cooked toor dal.
Simmer for 10 minutes and temper with crushed garlic and mustard seeds.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Avarekalu Saaru
steps: Pressure cook peeled hyacinth beans.
Grind coconut, garlic, and spices into a thick paste.
Boil the beans with the paste until thickened.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Mavinkayi Chitranna
steps: Grate raw mango and sauté with peanuts, turmeric, and chillies.
Mix the cooked, cooled rice into the mango tempering.
Garnish with coriander and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Haagalakai Gojju
steps: Sauté bitter gourd slices until brown.
Cook in tamarind juice and jaggery until the juice thickens.
Add rasam powder and sesame powder.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Alugadde Palya
steps: Boil, peel, and mash potatoes.
Sauté onions and chillies with turmeric; add potatoes.
Finish with lemon juice and coriander.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Sorekayi Kootu
steps: Cook bottle gourd and toor dal together.
Add a ground paste of coconut and cumin.
Garnish with roasted peanuts and mustard tempering.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Chitranna (Lemon Rice)
steps: Cook rice grains to be fluffy and let them cool completely.
Heat oil; sauté peanuts, mustard seeds, and urad dal until golden.
Add green chillies, curry leaves, and turmeric.
Turn off the flame and squeeze fresh lemon juice into the hot tempering.
Mix the tempering and salt into the cooled rice gently.
Garnish with fresh coriander and grated coconut.

recipes.name: Puliyogare
steps: Fresh Powder: Roast coriander seeds, fenugreek, sesame seeds, and 10 red chillies; grind into a fine powder.
Cook rice and spread on a wide plate to cool.
Boil tamarind juice with salt, jaggery, and the fresh prepared powder until it thickens into a paste (Gojju).
Sauté peanuts, dry coconut, and red chillies in oil.
Combine the Puliyogare Gojju and tempering with the rice.
Turn off the flame and let it sit for at least an hour for flavors to mature.

recipes.name: Massoppu Saaru
steps: Pressure cook mixed greens (spinach, dill, amaranth) and toor dal with garlic and chillies.
Fresh Spice Mix: Coarsely crush pepper and cumin seeds.
Mash the cooked greens and dal thoroughly into a creamy mixture.
Boil the mash with the fresh spice mix and salt.
Temper with mustard seeds and lots of crushed garlic in oil.
Turn off the flame; usually served with Ragi Mudde.

recipes.name: Heerekayi Thogave
steps: Pressure cook ridge gourd pieces and toor dal until soft.
Fresh Paste: Grind fresh coconut, green chillies, and a small piece of tamarind into a coarse paste.
Mash the gourd and dal slightly; add the fresh coconut paste and salt.
Simmer for 5 minutes until the consistency is thick.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Badanekayi Gojju
steps: Fire-roast or oil-fry brinjal until mushy; peel and mash.
Fresh Spice Powder: Dry roast sesame seeds and peanuts; grind into a coarse powder.
Simmer tamarind juice with jaggery, rasam powder, and salt.
Add mashed brinjal and the fresh sesame-peanut powder.
Temper with mustard seeds and dry red chillies.
Turn off the flame once the gravy thickens.

recipes.name: Curd Rice
steps: Overcook rice until very soft and mash it while hot.
Mix with milk and curd once cooled to prevent souring.
Temper with mustard, ginger, green chillies, and curry leaves.
Garnish with pomegranate seeds or grated carrot.

recipes.name: Maddur Vada
steps: Mix rice flour, maida, and rava with chopped onions, chillies, and curry leaves.
Add hot oil and a little water to knead into a stiff dough.
Flatten small portions into discs on a greased sheet.
Deep fry on medium flame until dark golden brown and crispy.
Drain excess oil and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Mangalore Buns
steps: Mash bananas with sugar; mix with curd, salt, and cumin.
Add maida to form a soft dough and rest for 6 hours.
Roll into thick small circles.
Deep fry until they puff up like golden balloons.
Drain oil and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Kosambari
steps: Soak moong dal for 1 hour and drain completely.
Mix with finely chopped cucumber, grated carrot, and coconut.
Heat a little oil, splutter mustard seeds and hing; pour over the mix.
Add salt, lemon juice, and coriander; mix gently.
Serve fresh as a healthy snack.

recipes.name: Obbattu (Holige)
steps: Boil dal until soft; grind with jaggery and cardamom into a thick paste (Puran).
Knead a very soft, elastic dough with maida, turmeric, and plenty of oil.
Stuff a ball of dal paste into a small portion of dough.
Roll thin on a greased sheet and toast on a hot tawa with ghee.
Turn off the flame once golden spots appear.

recipes.name: Kodubale
steps: Grind dry coconut and red chillies into a coarse powder.
Mix rice flour, roasted gram flour, and the coconut spice mix.
Add water to make a stiff dough and shape into small rings.
Deep fry on medium flame until the oil bubbles subside.
Drain and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Khara Sev
steps: Mix besan, rice flour, and spices into a soft dough.
Press through a sev mould directly into hot oil.
Fry for a minute until crisp (do not brown too much).
Remove, drain, and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Avalakki Mixture
steps: Deep fry poha in small batches until it puffs up.
Fry peanuts, roasted gram, and coconut slices separately until golden.
Toss everything together with salt, sugar, and turmeric while warm.
Add tempering of mustard and curry leaves; turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Banana Chips
steps: Peel bananas and slice very thin directly into a saltwater-turmeric solution.
Drain and pat dry completely.
Deep fry in hot coconut oil until crispy.
Remove, sprinkle extra salt if needed, and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Nippattu
steps: Coarsely crush peanuts and roasted gram.
Mix with flours, chilli powder, and hot oil; knead into a dough.
Flatten into thin discs and deep fry on low-medium flame.
Fry until they turn a deep golden color and become brittle.
Drain and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Vegetable Cutlet
steps: Boil and mash vegetables; mix with ginger-garlic paste and spices.
Shape into patties and dip in a thin flour slurry.
Coat with bread crumbs.
Shallow fry until both sides are dark golden brown.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Mirchi Bajji
steps: Slit chillies and remove seeds (optional).
Make a thick batter of besan, ajwain, salt, and water.
Dip each chilli to coat completely.
Deep fry until the outer layer is crisp and golden.
Drain and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Paddu (Paniyaram)
steps: Mix chopped onions, chillies, and ginger into the fermented batter.
Grease a paddu pan and pour batter into the holes.
Cook covered on medium flame; flip using a stick when the base is crisp.
Turn off the flame once both sides are golden brown.

recipes.name: Sweet Appam
steps: Mash bananas and mix with melted jaggery and rice flour.
Add cardamom powder to the thick batter.
Heat the paddu pan with ghee or oil.
Pour batter and fry until the exterior is dark brown and the center is soft.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Masala Vada (Ambode)
steps: Coarsely grind soaked chana dal without adding water.
Mix in chopped onions, dil leaves (sabbasige), and chillies.
Shape into flat patties and deep fry.
Fry until crunchy and golden brown.
Drain excess oil and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Kaara Pori (Kaara Pori)
steps: Heat oil and fry crushed garlic with skin until golden.
Add peanuts, dry coconut slices, and curry leaves; roast well.
Add turmeric, salt, and chilli powder; turn off the flame.
Immediately add puffed rice and toss vigorously until evenly coated and crisp.
Store in an airtight container.

recipes.name: Butter Murukku
steps: Mix rice flour, gram flour, cumin, and soft butter.
Knead into a dough and press through a murukku maker.
Fry until the murukku turns creamy golden and stops bubbling.
Drain and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Khara Boondi
steps: Pour a thin batter through a perforated ladle into hot oil.
Fry the tiny drops until crisp; drain.
Mix with fried peanuts, curry leaves, and chilli powder.
Toss well and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Peanut Sundal
steps: Pressure cook soaked peanuts with salt.
Temper oil with mustard, chillies, and curry leaves.
Add peanuts and sauté for 2 minutes.
Garnish with fresh coconut and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Rava Ladoo
steps: Roast rava in ghee until aromatic; grind sugar finely.
Mix rava, sugar, and cardamom powder.
Add warm melted ghee and fried cashews.
Bind into round balls while the mixture is still warm.
Turn off the flame once roasting is done.

recipes.name: Sweet Avalakki
steps: Rinse poha and drain water; let it soften for 5 minutes.
Mix with grated coconut, jaggery, and cardamom powder.
Add a drizzle of ghee and nuts if desired.
Serve as a quick tea-time snack.

recipes.name: Sajjige (Halwa)
steps: Roast rava in ghee until golden.
Add boiling water and cook until rava is soft.
Stir in sugar and cardamom; mix until it thickens and leaves the sides.
Garnish with fried nuts and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Vegetable Puff
steps: Sauté veggies with spices to make a dry stuffing.
Place stuffing inside pastry sheets and fold.
Bake in a preheated oven until golden and flaky.
Serve hot.

recipes.name: Roasted Chana
steps: Soak and boil chickpeas; pat them dry completely.
Toss with a little oil, salt, and turmeric.
Roast in a pan or oven until crunchy.
Turn off the flame and store.

recipes.name: Coconut Barfi
steps: Cook coconut and sugar together in a pan.
Stir continuously until the mixture thickens and reaches a soft ball stage.
Add ghee and cardamom; pour into a greased tray.
Turn off the flame, cool slightly, and cut into diamonds.

recipes.name: Banana Fritters (Podi)
steps: Peel and slice bananas lengthwise.
Prepare a thick batter of flour, sugar, and a pinch of salt.
Dip slices in batter and deep fry on medium heat.
Fry until golden brown and drain oil.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Ragi Mudde (Millet Ball)
steps: Bring 2 cups of water and salt to a rolling boil in a heavy pot.
Mix a little ragi flour with water to make a slurry and add to the pot.
Add the remaining ragi flour in the center; do not stir for 2 minutes.
Stir vigorously with a wooden stick (Mudde kolu) to remove lumps.
Steam on low heat for 5 minutes until the ragi flour is cooked.
Turn off the flame and roll into smooth balls with ghee-greased hands.

recipes.name: Avarekalu Saaru
steps: Roast coriander seeds, cinnamon, cloves, and red chillies; grind with coconut and garlic into a paste.
Pressure cook the hyacinth beans until tender.
Boil cooked beans with the ground masala paste and salt.
Simmer for 10 minutes until the raw smell of the masala disappears.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Akki Rotti
steps: Mix rice flour with finely chopped onion, grated carrot, dill leaves, green chillies, and salt.
Add warm water gradually to make a soft, pliable dough.
Pat a portion of dough thinly onto a cold, greased tawa by hand.
Cook on medium flame with oil until the edges turn golden and crisp.
Flip once to roast the other side for a minute; turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Vegetable Saagu
steps: Grind coconut, poppy seeds, fried gram, cloves, cinnamon, and green chillies into a smooth paste.
Boil mixed vegetables (carrot, beans, peas) with salt until tender.
Add the ground paste to the boiled vegetables and simmer for 5 minutes.
Heat oil and temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Pour the tempering into the saagu and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Donne Biryani (Veg)
steps: Grind mint, coriander, ginger, garlic, and green chillies into a green paste.
Heat oil and sauté marathi moggu, cloves, and cardamom.
Add mixed vegetables, the green paste, and soaked jeeraka samba rice; sauté for 2 minutes.
Add water (1:2 rice-to-water ratio) and salt; pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the flame and fluff the rice gently once the pressure is released.

recipes.name: Methi Pulao
steps: Grind coconut with green chillies and cumin seeds into a paste.
Heat oil and sauté cinnamon, cloves, and a large bunch of methi (fenugreek) leaves.
Add the ground coconut paste, soaked rice, and salt.
Pour in water (1:2 ratio) and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the flame and let it rest before fluffing.

recipes.name: Jolada Rotti
steps: Mix jowar flour with boiling water and salt using a spoon.
Knead into a very soft, smooth dough while the mixture is still warm.
Dust a surface with flour and pat a ball of dough into a thin circle.
Roast on a hot tawa, dabbing water on the top surface with a cloth.
Flip and cook until both sides have brown spots; turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Badanekayi Ennegayi
steps: Dry roast peanuts and sesame seeds; grind with garlic, tamarind, and salt into a thick paste.
Stuff slit small brinjals with this peanut-sesame masala paste.
Sauté onions in oil; place stuffed brinjals in the pan and cook covered on low flame.
Add any remaining paste and a little water; simmer until the oil separates.
Turn off the flame and serve with Jolada Rotti.

recipes.name: Hesaru Bele Khichdi
steps: Pressure cook rice and moong dal with turmeric and salt until very mushy.
Coarsely crush black pepper and cumin seeds.
Heat ghee and temper with crushed spices, ginger, and curry leaves.
Mix the tempering into the cooked rice-dal mash.
Turn off the flame and serve hot with coconut chutney.

recipes.name: Paddu (Gundponglu)
steps: Mix finely chopped onion, green chilli, ginger, and coriander into fermented dosa batter.
Heat a paddu pan and grease each cavity with oil.
Pour the batter into cavities and cook covered until the base is crisp.
Flip using a skewer and cook the other side until golden brown.
Turn off the flame and extract the paddus.

recipes.name: Akki Thari Uppittu
steps: Heat oil and temper with mustard, urad dal, peanuts, and green chillies.
Add 2.5 cups of water and salt; bring to a rolling boil.
Add 1 cup rice rava and a little cooked toor dal slowly while stirring.
Cook covered on low flame until the water is absorbed and grains are fluffy.
Stir in fresh grated coconut and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Bassaru (Greens Broth)
steps: Boil dill leaves and toor dal in excess water; strain and save the broth water.
Grind coconut, garlic, red chillies, and 2 tbsp of the cooked dal into a paste.
Mix the paste into the saved broth water with salt and boil for 5 minutes.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Turn off the flame and serve the liquid broth with Ragi Mudde.

recipes.name: Massoppu Saaru
steps: Pressure cook mixed greens (spinach, amaranth) and dal with garlic and green chillies.
Strain the water and mash the greens-dal mixture into a smooth paste.
Combine the mash with strained water, salt, and tamarind; bring to a boil.
Temper with mustard seeds and lots of crushed garlic in oil.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Tomato Bath
steps: Heat oil and sauté cinnamon, cloves, onions, and ginger-garlic paste.
Add chopped tomatoes and turmeric; cook until they become mushy.
Add washed rice and salt; sauté for a minute to coat the grains.
Add water (1:2 ratio) and pressure cook for 2 whistles.
Turn off the flame and fluff gently after the pressure is released.

recipes.name: Sorekayi Kootu
steps: Pressure cook diced bottle gourd and toor dal together until soft.
Grind coconut with cumin seeds and green chillies into a thick paste.
Mix the ground paste and salt into the gourd mixture and boil for 3 minutes.
Add roasted peanuts and temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Wheat Rava Upma
steps: Heat oil and temper mustard, urad dal, green chillies, and ginger.
Add chopped carrot and beans; sauté briefly, then add 2.5 cups water and salt.
Add wheat rava to the boiling water while stirring constantly.
Pressure cook for 2 whistles for a perfectly soft texture.
Turn off the flame and serve warm.

recipes.name: Neer Dosa
steps: Soak rice for 4 hours; grind with fresh coconut into a very thin, watery batter.
Add salt and extra water to reach a milk-like consistency.
Splash a ladle of batter onto a very hot, greased tawa and cover immediately.
Steam-cook for 1 minute (do not flip the dosa).
Fold into triangles, transfer to a plate, and turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Menthe Dosa (Fenugreek Dosa)
steps: Grind soaked rice, methi seeds, and poha; ferment the batter for 8 hours.
Add curd and salt to the batter just before cooking.
Pour a thick ladle of batter onto the pan; do not spread it thin.
Cover and cook without oil until the top is full of tiny pores.
Turn off the flame and serve with coconut chutney.

recipes.name: Chapati & Paneer Saagu
steps: Knead wheat flour with water and salt into a dough; roll and roast chapatis.
Grind coconut, poppy seeds, and cashews into a rich white paste.
Sauté whole spices, add the white paste, water, and simmer with paneer cubes.
Garnish with fresh coriander and salt.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Shavige Bath
steps: Steam or boil rice vermicelli until soft, drain completely, and set aside.
Heat oil; temper mustard, peanuts, urad dal, carrot, and beans.
Add salt and turmeric; mix in the steamed vermicelli gently.
Add fresh coriander and lemon juice; toss well.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Balekayi Podi (Banana Fry)
steps: Slice raw bananas into thin rounds and pat dry.
Coat the slices with a dry mixture of rice flour, chilli powder, salt, and hing.
Heat a tawa and shallow fry the slices with a little oil.
Cook until the exterior is crispy golden and the interior is soft.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Hesaru Bele Thove
steps: Cook moong dal with turmeric until it is very soft and creamy.
Heat ghee and temper with mustard seeds, grated ginger, and green chillies.
Stir the tempering and salt into the dal.
Add a squeeze of lemon juice and mix well.
Turn off the flame and serve with hot rice.

recipes.name: Huruli Kattu (Horse Gram Saaru)
steps: Boil horse gram and strain the water into a separate pot to use as broth.
Grind 2 tbsp cooked gram with pepper and garlic into a paste.
Add the paste, tamarind juice, and salt to the strained broth; boil well.
Temper with mustard seeds and curry leaves in oil.
Turn off the flame.

recipes.name: Mavinkayi Chitranna
steps: Cook rice grains to be separate and fluff them to cool completely.
Grate raw mango; sauté in oil with peanuts, mustard, turmeric, and chillies.
Add curry leaves and sauté until the mango bits are soft.
Mix this mango tempering and salt into the cooled rice gently.
Turn off the flame and garnish with fresh coconut.
